evidence: The grain size calculated from the full width at half-maximum (FWHM) of Ru(101) peaks using the Scherrer formula was increased as the deposition temperature increased from 220 to 300 °C (Table S1). The similar resistivity values of the films deposited in the temperature range within 220 −300 °C (Figure 4a) could therefore be also complemented from Scherrer’s analysis of the respective films. The density and roughness of the films deposited at 180, 220, and 300 °C were analyzed by XRR (Figure S4). The lowest density of 11.63 g cm−3 was obtained for the film deposited at 180 °C, which increased slightly to 11.89 g cm−3 at 220 °C and further increased to 12.25 g cm−3 at 300 °C, despite reaching the thermal decomposition temperature. These values were almost the same as the bulk value for Ru (12.37 g cm−3 72). The lowest roughness was observed for the sample deposited at 220 °C (1.465 nm) and higher for those deposited at 180 °C (1.671 nm) and 300 °C (1.801 nm).
